title: GenWave Theme Catalog Entry Metadata
description: The <slug>.meta.json shape for a kind:"theme" entry (app repo SPEC F103.2, catalog-owned). Mirrors persona-meta.schema.json's posture: additionalProperties is false — unlike the manifest, this document belongs entirely to the catalog, so an unrecognized field is a contributor mistake worth failing CI on, not a forward-compat concern. There is no samplePatter equivalent (themes have no on-air voice); in its place, `preview` is required — a small swatch payload the catalog shelf card renders without needing to fetch and parse the full manifest (T185's contract, defined here).
$comment: `added`'s pattern ends in (?![\s\S]), the same portable absolute-end-of-string anchor persona-meta.schema.json uses and documents in full there — repeated verbatim here rather than by reference so this file stands alone.

description.description: A short blurb introducing the theme's look and feel.

audience.description: Content self-rating, verified at PR review (mirrors persona-meta.schema.json's `audience`; a theme's colours/fonts alone are rarely mature, but the field stays uniform across both entry kinds so the shelf's rating logic never branches on `kind`).

added.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD) this entry was added to the catalog. `format: date` alone is annotation-only in draft-07 by default, so `pattern` carries the shape enforcement — but pattern alone only checks digit counts, not calendar validity; tools/validate.py separately parses this value with datetime.date.fromisoformat to reject a shape-valid but non-existent date.

preview.description: Shelf-card contract (T185): a HANDFUL of key token hex values per mode, enough to paint shelf chips (bg/surface/ink/accent/accent-2) without fetching and parsing the whole manifest. This is not the full token set and is never authoritative once a theme is installed — the manifest (`<slug>.theme.json`) remains the single source of truth for every token the app actually renders with; `preview` may drift from it (a stale swatch is a shelf cosmetic issue, not a broadcast one) and nothing here is re-validated against the manifest's own token values.

bestFor.description: Optional mood/use-case hints, e.g. "late-night", "high-contrast" — mirrors persona-meta.schema.json's `bestFor`.

swatchSet.description: The five shelf-chip swatches for one mode. Names match a subset of the manifest's own token vocabulary (ThemeModes token names) so a future automated preview-from-manifest generator can populate this object key-for-key.

hexColor.description: Same hex-colour shape as the app's ThemeManifestParser.TokenValuePattern (# followed by 3-8 hex digits) — kept in sync deliberately so a swatch value is never a shape the manifest itself couldn't carry.
